title: fix(contracts): match rule check patterns with a linear-time engine
body:
Title, branch and diff-excludes rule checks ran a repo admin's regular expression with the JavaScript engine against text the pull request author controls. Patterns like `\d+\d+\d+x` or `(a+)+` take minutes on a long line, and under JavaScriptCore's backtrack limit can silently report no match.

## What changed

- Rule patterns compile and match with `re2js` (RE2 port, linear time), in the contract's `pattern()` validator and in the workflow's rule evaluation. Lookaround and backreferences are rejected when a pack is saved, with a message naming the check; everything RE2 accepts runs in time proportional to the input.
- The validator compiles each pattern once per check per pull request; no scan cap is needed.

## Verification

- `bun run check`; contract and workflow logic tests, including `(?<=a)b` and `(a)\1` rejected, `^(a+)+$`, `^[a-z]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*$`, `(\d{3}-)+`, `^(feat|fix)(\(.+\))?: .+` and the recommended pack accepted, and `\d+\d+\d+x` against 2,000 digits finishing in under 250 ms.
- Portal build and hub OpenAPI test pass.

Closes CL-XXXX
